doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lincoln Center and jazz
summary: John Lewis's complaint, and the change since Wynton's prominence.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: We’re sitting across from the Lincoln Center. What has been its role in the popularity or burgeoning reemergence? Well, I don’t know, you left in the sixties, and now we’re in the nineties…

Lincoln Center was here, but I remember one guy then, a drummer around town named John Lewis, and he told me one day, “This is really a disgrace that they built this Lincoln Center here and they had one building for this kind of music and one building for that kind of music and one building for theater and one building for cinema, but there’s nothing there for jazz, and that’s the music of this country. Why didn’t they build a building for jazz?” They have an occasional, only occasional, jazz concert until Wynton’s prominence came into the thing. That’s the reality of it.
Which made possible your featured concert there.
Yeah, that’s a big deal. Have a featured concert at Lincoln Center.
